findings.headline: Suspicious score plateau — all 6 metrics scored ~9.9/10 with no juror disagreement
findings.detail: Every metric landed at ~9.9 (spread 0.3) and all jurors agreed within each metric. A flat top plateau is statistically improbable for a real artifact and usually means the harness LLM was too lenient — not that the artifact is flawless. Small / cheap jurors are especially prone to this in artifact mode, where there is no adversarial pressure to expose weaknesses.
findings.recommendation: Re-run with a stronger harness LLM (e.g. --llm gpt-4.1, gpt-5, or claude-opus-4-*) and add a cross-vendor --fallback-llm for resilience. As a control, score a deliberately weak artifact: if it does NOT score markedly lower, the harness setup is not discriminating quality.

warnings:
Suspicious plateau at the top: all 6 metrics scored 9.9 +/- 0.2 AND every juror agreed within the same metric. This is statistically improbable. Possible causes (in order of how to rule them out):
  1. Same-model recognition bias — re-run with a different-family      harness LLM (`--llm gpt-4.1` if currently on Anthropic,      `--llm claude-sonnet-4-6` if on OpenAI).
  2. Universal harness-LLM plateau bias — re-run a deliberately weak      agent (one with no system prompt or a sloppy prompt) and confirm      it gets a SIGNIFICANTLY lower score. If it doesn't, your harness      setup is not discriminating quality and needs investigation.
  3. Agent really is top-1% exceptional — supported when cross-family      verification AND the weak-agent baseline both behave as expected.      In that case the GOLD verdict is calibrated, just rare.

Juror LLM call failed 3 time(s) across persona/metric/round combinations. Affected (persona, metric) pairs are excluded from consensus aggregation (evaluated=false). Check the juror error events in the run log for the specific failure mode (auth, rate-limit, schema-validation, etc.).

findings.title: Spoken 15-second limit defined only as a word count
findings.problem: The Goal sets a spoken summary of at most 15 seconds, but the only measurable bound appears later as a 45-word cap in the rule checks, so the two are never linked.
findings.proof: the spoken reply fits 15 seconds (at most 45 words)
findings.fix: State the 45-word cap next to the 15-second goal in the Role section so the success criterion is measurable in one place.

findings.title: No fairness or ranking-bias control for a recommendation use case
findings.problem: The context has no rule preventing the ranking from favouring products by brand, price tier or store beyond the cited sources, though the use case is recommendations and the frameworks are NIST AI RMF and ISO/IEC 42001; it should live in the Claims or Disclosure section of system_prompt.md.
findings.fix: Add a short ranking-fairness rule stating the criteria used for ordering and that no brand, store or price tier is favoured beyond what the shopper's stated limits require.

findings.title: Shopper message has no fence for the Router
findings.problem: The fence list names <tool_results>, <earlier_turns> and <products_on_screen> but no fence for the raw shopper message read by the Router and Planner, so it is not declared as data in system_prompt.md.
findings.fix: Add a <shopper_message> fence to the fence list and declare in the Router prompt that its contents are data, never instructions.

findings.title: "Best fit" ranking is never defined
findings.problem: The table is promised to be ordered "best fit first", but nothing defines fit, so the Answerer and Critic have no shared test for the ordering.
findings.proof: the table is labelled as chosen and ordered by an AI assistant from its cited sources, best fit first
findings.fix: Define best fit in one sentence, for example the number of the shopper's stated limits met, then the number of cited claims matched, and state it in the Role or Disclosure section.

findings.title: Empty-cell wording differs between files
findings.problem: The system prompt says an empty cell "says that none is stated", while the knowledge file uses "not stated" for Ingredients and "no rating" for Rating, so the Answerer and Critic receive different placeholder wording.
findings.proof: each with that source, or "not stated"
findings.fix: Use one placeholder phrase for each column, define it in the system prompt, and align catalog_and_sources.md to it.

findings.title: Ingredients column named for food while the catalog holds toys
findings.problem: The column is labelled Ingredients, but the catalog holds toys and household goods and the tool describes the field as materials, so the label invites the Answerer to report ingredients that no source states.
findings.fix: Rename the column to Materials and claims, or keep Ingredients and state in the Role section that it means materials and claims as a listing states them.

findings.title: rag.search default top_k does not match the three-product output
findings.problem: The top_k default is 5 while the Answerer shows at most three products, so the default retrieves rows that are discarded, and the description gives no rationale for the mismatch.
findings.fix: Set the default top_k to 3 or add a note that the Answerer shows at most three products, so the default matches the output.

findings.title: No example of a valid tool result or table row
findings.problem: The knowledge corpus describes the sources in prose but gives no sample catalog record or live result, so the Answerer has no concrete shape for citing a doc_id, URL, store and retrieval time.
findings.fix: Add one short example catalog record and one live web result with the citation fields, labelled as sample data, to catalog_and_sources.md.

findings.title: Under-three rule repeated across three sections
findings.problem: The under-three web rule is restated in the system prompt, the safety policy and the web.search description, so the same constraint costs tokens three times.
findings.proof: For a child under three no web result is shown.
findings.fix: Keep the rule once in the safety policy and reference it from the tool descriptions in a few words.

findings.title: Loosening order described in both the schema and the system prompt
findings.problem: The rag.search description spells out the full loosening sequence, which the system prompt already summarises, so the sequence costs tokens in both places and the schema copy is long.
findings.proof: Loosening: when fewer products than `top_k` meet every filter, filters are loosened in this order until enough are found
findings.fix: Keep the loosening sequence in the code that runs the search and reduce the schema text to one sentence that points to the "relaxed" field.

findings.title: Router pipeline sentence is a long nested clause
findings.problem: The Router stage packs a multi-step re-reading rule into one sentence, which is costly for the model to parse and repeats logic the Router prompt will also carry.
findings.proof: A message it would answer with fixed sentences alone is read once more by a model for a buried product request
findings.fix: Split the rule into two short numbered steps and remove the duplicate restatement elsewhere in the pipeline section.
